rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent torqued, pinched stack with a recognizable dominant gesture in all four views. The massing has a clear primary body with secondary projecting plates, so hierarchy is present, though some edge fragments weaken the legibility. It avoids being purely stair-stepped, but the composition still leans on layered plate offsets rather than a fully resolved volumetric twist. The void logic is limited: there is some undercut/pinch potential, but no strong public courtyard or carve-out that clearly anchors the mass. Repair integrity is only moderate because several protrusions and clipped corners suggest a form that may have been over-edited or would need simplification. Overall it resonates well with torqued-stack precedents, especially in the Vancouver House / tower family, without feeling like a direct copy.
warnings: The undercut/void is present only weakly; it does not yet read as a meaningful public void.
Some peripheral slivers and offsets make the mass feel lightly over-articulated.
A cleaner central anchor would improve cross-view consistency.
